questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a worked example, which conditions give monobromination of a ketone at the alpha position under basic control?

options.misconception: excess base leads to polyhalogenation

options.text: One equivalent of base and bromine at low temperature

options.misconception: acid conditions give a different rate law
enolate formation requires base

questions.explanation: With one equivalent of base at low temperature, a single enolate forms and reacts once with bromine; excess base promotes successive halogenation because alpha hydrogens become more acidic after each substitution.
questions.hint: Controlled enolate formation limits bromination.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: On an exam, what product class forms when acetaldehyde undergoes base-catalyzed aldol addition?

options.misconception: that requires dehydration of the aldol
that requires oxidation
that requires alcohol and acid

questions.explanation: Base-catalyzed aldol addition gives a beta-hydroxy aldehyde, which can dehydrate on heating to the conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde; the addition product itself is the beta-hydroxy compound.
questions.hint: Aldol addition gives a beta-hydroxy carbonyl.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the reaction under study, what product forms when ethyl acetate undergoes a Claisen condensation?

options.misconception: that is the aldol analogue
that requires hydrolysis
that requires dehydration

questions.explanation: Two esters condense under alkoxide base to give a beta-keto ester, with alkoxide expulsion from the acyl substitution step and a final deprotonation that drives the equilibrium forward.
questions.hint: Claisen gives a beta-keto ester.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Think through the following: which structural motif is required of a Michael acceptor?

options.misconception: it must be conjugated
that is not a Michael acceptor
that lacks the conjugated pi system

questions.explanation: A Michael acceptor is an electron-poor alkene conjugated to a carbonyl, so the beta carbon is electrophilic and a nucleophile adds there in a conjugate 1,4-addition.
questions.hint: Conjugated enones accept Michael donors.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Review question: which conditions favor formation of the kinetic enolate?

options.misconception: that favors the thermodynamic enolate
that may not form the enolate fully
acid does not give lithium enolates

questions.explanation: A bulky strong base such as LDA at low temperature removes the most accessible alpha proton quickly, giving the kinetic enolate, whereas equilibrating conditions favor the more substituted thermodynamic enolate.
questions.hint: Bulky and cold gives kinetic control.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a practice problem, which two reactions make up a Robinson annulation?

options.misconception: that omits the Michael step
that gives a different ring system

options.text: Michael addition followed by intramolecular aldol

options.misconception: that is unrelated

questions.explanation: A Robinson annulation combines a Michael addition of an enolate to an enone with a subsequent intramolecular aldol condensation, forming a new six-membered ring with an alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone.
questions.hint: Michael then intramolecular aldol builds the ring.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: When analyzing the transformation, what class of compound is prepared by alkylation of diethyl malonate followed by hydrolysis and decarboxylation?

options.misconception: that comes from acetoacetic ester synthesis
that comes from a Grignard addition
decarboxylation gives the acid

questions.explanation: Malonic ester synthesis installs an alkyl group on the alpha carbon, then hydrolysis and decarboxylation give a substituted acetic acid with the new group on the carbon adjacent to the carboxyl.
questions.hint: Malonic ester gives substituted acetic acids.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a tutorial session, what class of compound results from alkylating ethyl acetoacetate followed by hydrolysis and decarboxylation?

options.misconception: that is the malonic ester product
the carbonyl retains a methyl group
no reduction is performed

questions.explanation: Acetoacetic ester synthesis gives a substituted methyl ketone after hydrolysis and decarboxylation because the remaining acetyl fragment becomes the methyl ketone carbonyl.
questions.hint: Acetoacetic ester gives methyl ketones.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: You are given the following: which statement about keto-enol tautomerism is correct?

options.text: The enol is always more stable
options.misconception: most simple enols are less stable

options.text: The keto form usually predominates for simple ketones

options.misconception: tautomers differ only in proton and pi-bond placement

options.text: The equilibrium is catalyzed only by strong acid
options.misconception: both acid and base catalyze it

questions.explanation: For simple carbonyl compounds the keto tautomer is favored because the carbon-oxygen double bond is stronger than the carbon-carbon double bond of the enol, though enols can be stabilized by conjugation or hydrogen bonding.
questions.hint: Keto is usually more stable than enol.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a synthesis planning session, why does heating an aldol product favor dehydration?

options.misconception: water is formed but conjugation is the driver
the carbonyl is retained

options.text: Conjugation with the carbonyl stabilizes the enone product
The aldol is unstable to light
options.misconception: heat, not light, promotes dehydration

questions.explanation: Dehydration of a beta-hydroxy carbonyl gives an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl whose pi system is conjugated with the carbonyl, providing thermodynamic stabilization that drives the elimination, especially on heating.
questions.hint: Conjugated enone is more stable.
